title: Divisibility Rules 2–11
summary: Tell whether a number divides exactly without dividing: look at the last digit for $2$, $5$ and $10$, the digit sum for $3$ and $9$, the last two digits for $4$, the last three for $8$, and the alternating digit sum for $11$. Use the same tests to find remainders.
bigIdeas: Only part of a number decides whether it divides by $2$, $4$, $5$, $8$ or $10$: the end.
For $3$ and $9$ the digit sum decides, because $10$, $100$, $1000$… are each one more than a multiple of $9$.
tips: Even numbers end in $0$, $2$, $4$, $6$ or $8$, and divide by $2$.
Add the digits: if the sum divides by $3$ (or $9$), so does the number. $471$: $4 + 7 + 1 = 12$, so $3$ divides it.
Only the last two digits decide $4$: $7316$ divides by $4$ because $16$ does.
Divisible by $6$ means even and divisible by $3$.
